topPRs.title: op-reth: drop the RPC replay override and pin the executor-routing fork
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Alternative to #23670 for ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485, paired with ethereum-optimism/reth#33 (the fork backport of paradigmxyz/reth#28266's executor routing, finishing George's ethereum-optimism/reth#24).

With the fork replaying every block transaction through the block executor, op-reth needs no RPC override: this branch is #23670's integration tests and Lagoon fixtures on top of develop, pinned to the reth fork head `bff7be24` that carries the executor routing. The three canonical settlement tests, the refund-dependent affordability case and both raw-block cases pass against that pin with no `Trace` or `Call` implementation in op-reth; the same canonical tests fail on develop against the current `op-v2.6.0-1` tag, which is the regression they pin. All-features clippy on `reth-optimism-rpc` and `reth-optimism-node` is clean.

One #23670 test case changes shape: the fork's `inspect_transaction_in_block` is now index-based and takes no transaction environment, so the "supplied environment" case becomes a direct replay of index 2 that asserts the settled receipt gas. Raw `debug_traceBlock` and `debug_traceBadBlock` stay on the bare EVM in the fork, so the raw-block cases keep asserting pre-refund gas.

The reth pin moves to the merged fork tag before this lands; after it merges, both op-reth-premium workspaces repin to the merge commit. Review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`, `reth-update-reviewer`) run before this leaves draft; findings and dismissals are recorded here.

topPRs.title: op-reth: settle SDM refunds during canonical RPC replay
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Related to ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485. Canonical transaction and block replays include SDM settlement, so debug gas, replayed balances/state diffs, and intermediate roots agree with execution. This is an independent line of work based on George’s #23615/#23616, with canonical versus diagnostic replay separated and the supplied transaction environment preserved.

Depends on ethereum-optimism/reth#26. The temporary PR-head pin must be replaced with the merged fork tag before merging this PR. Raw/bad-block tracing keeps its existing permissive, pre-refund behavior; parity call-frame gas keeps its existing convention.

Adds imported multi-transaction coverage, an unrefunded gap, refund-dependent affordability, modified-environment replay, direct OTS/call-many checks, and traceChain success/error alignment. CI op-reth integration tests pass: 81 passed and one skipped, including both multi-transaction settlement regressions. Nightly formatting passes. CI workspace tests, clippy, builds, documentation, and Rust merge gates pass on the latest push; two Go end-to-end memory jobs remain pending. The prerequisite’s helper unit tests and workspace all-features clippy pass. Mirror checker unit tests pass, while existing stale mirror entries still fail its repository-wide check.

Static Rust and pin/deposit reviews were performed. Full workspace, JS-tracer feature, and forward-upstream-release reviews have not been run; this pin adds only the prerequisite RPC commit to the existing fork release.

topPRs.title: op-node,op-deployer,kona: run OP Private chains in follow mode with no source
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23717, which is stacked on #23657.

This adds `settlement_chain_id` to the rollup config:
- 0 or absent on a public chain;
- the chain's own ID on a settlement chain;
- the settlement chain's ID on a private chain.

op-deployer fills it from the same `settlementChainId` deploy override that #23657 writes into the `ChainConfig` predeploy. It omits the field when it is 0, so a public chain's `rollup.json` is unchanged. op-node only parses the field, because it uses `DisallowUnknownFields`.

**kona-node on a private chain:**
- **No L1 derivation.** It uses the delegated (follow-mode) derivation actor. With no `--l2.follow.source`, the actor has no provider ("follow mode with nothing to follow"). Nothing ever updates safe or finalized, so they stay at genesis. There is no code that turns the safe head off.
- **Engine reset.** `find_starting_forkchoice` still walks unsafe back to a canonical L1 origin. A private chain has no sequencing window and never posts batches, so it skips the sequencing-window safe search. It keeps the EL's persisted safe and finalized heads, capped at unsafe. Without this, a restart or reset either moves safe off genesis once the chain is a window old, or walks every block back to genesis, which stalls the sequencer for a time that grows with chain age. Public chains go through the same code as before.
- **safedb.** `--safedb.path` is rejected on a private chain, as it already is with a follow source, because nothing would ever write it.

Known and left as is:
- **Follower warnings.** The sequencer reports `current_l1` as zero. A following RPC node therefore warns about an L1 inconsistency every 4 seconds and keeps its safe head at genesis.
- **L1 deposits.** A private chain still includes L1 deposits from its OptimismPortal. That is deferred to the deposits milestone.

Tests:
- kona: the role check, serde (omitted when 0, absent reads as 0), and an actor with no provider never sending a safe or finalized head. A strict-mock set covers `find_starting_forkchoice`: a private chain keeps its safe head and walks nothing, a public chain is unchanged, and the cap applies when unsafe rewinds below safe. There is also a safedb rejection test.
- op-node: JSON parse.
- op-deployer: `CombineDeployConfig`. `TestL2GenesisAllocsInvariants` checks that the rollup config matches the `ChainConfig` slot in every mode.
- `cargo nextest` on kona-engine, kona-node-service and kona-node: 370 passed. Clippy, nightly fmt, gofmt, vet and op-golangci-lint are clean.

topPRs.title: kona-proofs: Test multi-chain Lagoon activation and CrossL2Inbox access list enforcement
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage` finds an undeclared message from the gas cost of one SLOAD of the checksum slot. A compiler that removes the SLOAD lets every message through. A future fork that changes SLOAD gas pricing can also break the threshold. Production chains get CrossL2Inbox from frozen NUT bundles, and op-reth runs them.

`TestActivationBlockNUTBundle` now runs each bundled fork from Lagoon onward with a dependency set of 1 chain and of 2 chains. With 2 chains, Lagoon activates the interop contracts. The kona programs get the sequencer's dependency set, so kona-client proves the same block.

The multi-chain case checks the setFeature and ETHLiquidity funding deposits and the interop state. It calls `validateMessage` on the CrossL2Inbox proxy with `eth_call`. Without an access list, the call must revert with exactly `NotInAccessList()`. With the checksum declared for the proxy, the call must succeed.

From Lagoon onward, `just nut-prefork-state-for <fork>` also writes `<fork>_multichain_state.json`, and `check-nut-locks` requires it. The next fork's multi-chain case boots from it.

The change affects tests and tooling only. ethereum-optimism/optimism#23890 adds the matching acceptance-test checks.
